name: Arabica Atelier
tagline: A specialty café for aesthetes: tasting flights, rare lots and a brew bar

listing.description: A website for a specialty café, wine or tea bar: a restrained serif, a lot-by-lot menu card, gallery and reviews.

seo.title: Arabica Atelier — specialty coffee and tastings in Tashkent
seo.description: Three-lot tasting flights, pour-over, siphon and AeroPress, rare Geshas and anaerobic processes. A café at 158 Buyuk Ipak Yuli St, Tuesday to Sunday.
seo.answer: Arabica Atelier is a specialty café at 158 Buyuk Ipak Yuli St (Mirzo-Ulugbek), open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00–21:00. Pour-over starts at 36,000 UZS, a three-lot tasting flight is 95,000 UZS, Gesha 85,000 UZS a cup. Barista-led tastings run on Saturdays by booking.

sections.title: Coffee to taste, not just to drink
sections.subtitle: Twelve lots from farmers in Ethiopia, Colombia and Panama, a brew bar and three-cup flights — to feel how the same coffee changes with the method.

sections.label: Atelier
sections.title: Slow coffee
sections.text: There are no syrups or big cups at the atelier. There are scales accurate to a tenth of a gram, water with tuned mineral content and a barista who will tell you why an Ethiopian lot smells of jasmine. We’re open to people who want to understand coffee — and to those who just want a very good cup.

items.title: Fragrance
items.text: Smell six dry grounds and guess the origins.

items.title: The crust
items.text: Pour, wait four minutes, break the crust.

items.title: Spoons
items.text: Taste each lot as it cools — the flavour opens up.

items.title: Choice
items.text: Take home your favourite lot in beans at 15% off.

items.quote: For the first time I realised coffee can smell of strawberries. Now I go to every cupping.
items.author: Dilnoza A.

items.quote: The Gesha is pricey, but it’s the best coffee I’ve had in Tashkent.
items.author: Otabek R.

items.a: 120,000 UZS, about an hour and a half, up to 8 people. Book via the button on the site.

items.q: Do I need to know about coffee?
items.a: No, the barista explains everything from scratch.
Yes, cappuccino and cortado, but no syrups.
Every lot on the list, in 200 g bags, from 150,000 UZS.
